# x86 machine options without code generation of their own

GCC 16.2 has 666 spellings of x86 `-m` options (`gcc --completion=-m`). The driver has an arm for
the ones it implements: the ISA options and `-march=`/`-mtune=` (docs/x86-isa-permissions-and-simd-abi.md),
the code models, the stack-protector guard, the retpoline and return thunks, `-mharden-sls=`,
`-mregparm=`, `-mpreferred-stack-boundary=`, the `-pg` family, `-mno-red-zone`, `-mno-80387`,
`-mgeneral-regs-only` and so on. This table is the rest: every spelling none of those arms takes,
with what the driver does with it in each mode and why.

The words:

* **accepted**: in silence. What is asked is what the compiler does, with or without the option.
* **hint**: accepted with a warning that nothing acts on it. The option chooses among ways of
  generating equivalent code. `LCCC_STRICT_OPTIONS=1` makes it an error, so that a capability probe
  can tell it from an option that is implemented.
* **ignored, with GCC's warning**: GCC 16.2 accepts the option, warns and does nothing; so does lccc,
  in the same words.
* **implemented**: the option has its effect (an arm of the driver; listed here so that the table is
  the whole list).
* **depends**: decided by the rest of the command line; the rule is given below the table.
* **refused**: an error that says why. Accepting the option would produce something other than what
  was asked for: another layout or calling convention, a mitigation that is not there, an object
  without the record it should carry.
* **error, as in GCC**: GCC 16.2 refuses the spelling in that mode; lccc refuses it in GCC's words.

An `-mno-NAME` whose name GCC 16.2 does not have is accepted as before (nothing by that name exists
here to switch off) and refused under `LCCC_STRICT_MFLAGS`; an `-mNAME` GCC does not have is an error.

Verdicts in the table, counted per spelling and mode: 118 state, 119 hint, 11 ignored, 38 effect, 8 depends, 106 refused, 8 invalid.

`scripts/gen_x86_mflag_policy.py --check --lccc BIN --gcc gcc-16` holds every row to the compiler
and the whole of GCC's list to the table.

### The rows that depend on the command line

* `crc32`: `-mcrc32` is accepted where SSE4.2 is enabled and refused where it is not; `-mno-crc32` is accepted where SSE4.2 is not enabled and refused where it is. GCC has a CRC32 bit of its own; here `__CRC32__` and the permission to call the intrinsics are SSE4.2's.
* `mwait`: `-mmwait` is accepted where SSE3 is enabled and refused where it is not; `-mno-mwait` the other way round. GCC has a MWAIT bit of its own; here `_mm_monitor` and `_mm_mwait` are SSE3's.

## `-mNAME=VALUE`

| option | value | |
|---|---|---|
| `-mabi=` | `ms` | **refused**: it makes the Microsoft calling convention the default for every function; LCCC implements that convention for functions declared `ms_abi` only |
| `-mabi=` | `sysv` | accepted: functions have the System V calling convention unless they are declared otherwise |
| `-mabi=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |
| `-maddress-mode=` | `long` | x86-64: accepted: addresses are 64-bit<br>IA-32: error, as in GCC: "address mode 'long' not supported in the 32 bit mode" |
| `-maddress-mode=` | `short` | x86-64: error, as in GCC: "address mode 'short' not supported in the 64 bit mode"<br>IA-32: accepted: addresses are 32-bit |
| `-maddress-mode=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |
| `-main=` | any | GCC's warning that the option is for Cobol, and nothing else |
| `-malign-data=` | `abi` | accepted: an object has at least its psABI alignment |
| `-malign-data=` | `cacheline` | hint: more alignment than the psABI asks for is a preference, and no object depends on another translation unit having it |
| `-malign-data=` | `compat` | accepted: an object has at least its psABI alignment; GCC's default |
| `-malign-data=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |
| `-mapx-features=` | any | `none`, or any `-mno-apx-features=` list, is accepted while APX is off (`-mapxf` not in force); otherwise refused: APX code generation is selected as a whole by `-mapxf`, its features cannot be chosen one by one. Any list but `none` is an error on IA-32, in GCC's words |
| `-masm=` | `att` | accepted: the output and the `asm` templates are in AT&T syntax |
| `-masm=` | `intel` | **refused**: it switches the output and the dialect of `asm` templates to Intel syntax; LCCC writes and reads AT&T syntax only |
| `-masm=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |
| `-mbranch-cost=` | any | 0 to 5: a hint. Anything else is GCC's error |

| `-mfentry-name=` | any | implemented: the function a `-pg -mfentry` site calls. An empty name is GCC's error |
| `-mfentry-section=` | any | implemented: the section of the `-mrecord-mcount` records |

| `-mmove-max=` | `128` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mmove-max=` | `256` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mmove-max=` | `512` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mmove-max=` | `none` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mmove-max=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |
| `-mno-ain=` | any | GCC's warning that the option is for Cobol, and nothing else |
| `-mno-apx-features=` | any | `none`, or any `-mno-apx-features=` list, is accepted while APX is off (`-mapxf` not in force); otherwise refused: APX code generation is selected as a whole by `-mapxf`, its features cannot be chosen one by one. Any list but `none` is an error on IA-32, in GCC's words |
| `-mrecip=` | any | a list of `all`, `default`, `none`, `div`, `sqrt`, `vec-div`, `vec-sqrt`, each with or without `!`: a hint (reciprocal estimates are never generated). Anything else is GCC's error |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `byte_loop` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `libcall` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `loop` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `rep_4byte` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `rep_8byte` | x86-64: hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it<br>IA-32: error, as in GCC: "'-mstringop-strategy=rep_8byte' not supported for 32-bit code" |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `rep_byte` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `unrolled_loop` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | `vector_loop` | hint: a choice among ways of generating the same code; nothing in the object, the ABI or the language depends on it |
| `-mstringop-strategy=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |
| `-mtune-ctrl=` | any | any value: a hint. GCC checks the value against its tuning tables; LCCC has none |
| `-mveclibabi=` | `acml` | hint: a permission to call a vector math library; no such call is generated |
| `-mveclibabi=` | `aocl` | hint: a permission to call a vector math library; no such call is generated |
| `-mveclibabi=` | `svml` | hint: a permission to call a vector math library; no such call is generated |
| `-mveclibabi=` | any other | error, as in GCC: "unrecognized argument in option" |

## Other names for options

GCC 16.2 keeps these as names for another option and warns; lccc prints the same warning and reads
the other option in their place.

| option | stands for | warning |
|---|---|---|
| `-mfused-madd` | `-ffp-contract=fast` | "'-mfused-madd' is deprecated; use '-ffp-contract=' instead" |
| `-mintel-syntax` | `-masm=intel` | "'-mintel-syntax' and '-mno-intel-syntax' are deprecated; use '-masm=intel' and '-masm=att' instead" |
| `-mno-fused-madd` | `-ffp-contract=off` | "'-mfused-madd' is deprecated; use '-ffp-contract=' instead" |
| `-mno-intel-syntax` | `-masm=att` | "'-mintel-syntax' and '-mno-intel-syntax' are deprecated; use '-masm=intel' and '-masm=att' instead" |
| `-mno-sse5` | `-mno-avx` | "'-msse5' was removed" |
| `-msse5` | `-mavx` | "'-msse5' was removed" |
| `-mstore-max=V` | `-mmove-max=V` | "'-mstore-max=' is deprecated; use '-mmove-max=' instead" |
| `-malign-functions=N` | `-falign-functions=2^N`, where no `-falign-functions` is given; N from 0 to 16, 0 for the default | "'-malign-functions' is obsolete, use '-falign-functions'" |
| `-malign-jumps=N` | `-falign-jumps=2^N`, where no `-falign-jumps` is given; N from 0 to 16, 0 for the default | "'-malign-jumps' is obsolete, use '-falign-jumps'" |
| `-malign-loops=N` | `-falign-loops=2^N`, where no `-falign-loops` is given; N from 0 to 16, 0 for the default | "'-malign-loops' is obsolete, use '-falign-loops'" |
